subject: mathematics
question_text: Decide with justification whether f: (0, ∞)→R defined by f(x) = log x is an injection, a surjection or a bijection.

mark_split.label: Proof that f is one one

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.11, chapter 2 FUNCTIONS, Very Short Answer question 18(iv). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape gives one mark to the one one argument and one to the onto argument, because the question asks for both and a student who proves only one still earns half. The verdict line carries no mark and is authored for the student, not for the examiner. The stem prints log x without naming a base; it is read here as logₑ x, the Intermediate default, and the answer line says so on the page. The verdict does not depend on the choice: for any base a > 0 with a ≠ 1 the same two arguments run with aʸ in place of eʸ, and the map is still a bijection. The domain and codomain answered against are the ones printed in the stem, (0, ∞) and R. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1–Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would decide this — how you prove one one for a logarithm, and how you find a pre-image for any real y.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Prove f is one one
steps.margin_note: First mark. Copy the domain and the codomain from the question first. Then subtract the two logarithms and use log a − log b = log(a/b).
steps.memory_tip: Subtract the two logs to get log(a/b) = 0, and log of a number is 0 only when that number is 1.
lines: f: (0, ∞)→R, f(x) = log x, base e
Let f(a) = f(b), where a, b > 0
⇒ log a = log b ⇒ log a − log b = 0

recall.must_convey: That log a = log b gives log(a/b) = 0, so a/b = 1 and a = b, which is what one one means.
accept: let f of a equal f of b then log a equals log b so log of a by b is zero and a by b is one so a equals b
subtract the logarithms to get log of a over b equal to zero then a equals b
take exponentials on both sides of log a equals log b to get a equals b
log a equals log b anukunte a equals b vastundi so one one
the logarithm sends different positive numbers to different values so it is injective
reject: the log graph is increasing so it is one one
I prove it is an injection

steps.why: log a − log b = log(a/b) turns the assumption into a single logarithm, and log of a number is 0 only when that number is 1. Both a and b are positive, so dividing them is allowed.
common_mistakes: Writing log a − log b = log a / log b, which is not a logarithm law.
Saying it is one one because the curve rises, with no algebra.

steps.label: Prove f is onto
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Start from an arbitrary y in R, including negative y, and produce eʸ. It is positive for every real y, so it lies in the domain (0, ∞).
steps.memory_tip: eʸ is positive for every real y, negative y included, so the pre-image is always inside (0, ∞).
lines: Solve log x = y ⇒ x = eʸ
eʸ > 0 for every real y, so x ∈ (0, ∞)
∴ every y ∈ R has a pre-image; f is onto.

recall.must_convey: That for an arbitrary real y the number e to the power y is positive, lies in the domain (0, ∞), and has log equal to y, so every element of R is reached.
accept: take any y in R then x equals e to the power y is positive so it is in the domain and log of it is y
solve log x equals y to get x equals e power y which is always positive
every real number is the logarithm of some positive number so the map is onto
e power y eppudu positive so x domain lo untundi and log x equals y
for each y in R there is a positive x with log x equal to y
reject: I prove it is a surjection

steps.why: Onto means nothing in R is left out, and R includes negative numbers. Producing eʸ shows the pre-image exists for those too, because eʸ is positive for every real y and so sits inside the domain (0, ∞).
common_mistakes: Writing only 'the range of log is R' with no x produced for a general y.
Thinking a negative y has no pre-image; e to a negative power is still positive.

steps.label: State the verdict
steps.margin_note: No separate mark, but write it. The question named three words, so the last line must pick one and tie it to the two proofs.
steps.memory_tip: One one and onto together is the definition of a bijection, so name both before the verdict.
lines: f is one one and onto.

recall.must_convey: That f is a bijection BECAUSE it was shown to be both one one and onto on the stated domain and codomain.
accept: since f is one one and onto it is a bijection
both parts hold so log x from zero infinity to R is bijective
it is an injection and a surjection so it is a bijection
one one and onto rendu unnai so f bijection

steps.why: The question offered three words, so the answer must choose one and tie it to the two proofs above. Because f is a bijection here, its inverse eˣ from R to (0, ∞) exists.
common_mistakes: Naming only 'injection' when both properties were proved.
Stopping after the two arguments and never writing the verdict.
